name: The Japanese Oak in Jephson Gardens

location.address: Jephson Gardens, Newbold Terrace / The Parade, Royal Leamington Spa

access: Free, public park (Green Flag, council-run), open daily; entrances on Newbold Terrace and The Parade. Opening hours not checked in this pass.
verify_notes: Council record (owner of the ground, Warwick District Council "Trees at Jephson's" project): Quercus acuta, native to Japan; says it "may be one of the finest Japanese oaks in the country" and is best looked at from the bottom of the steps. Evergreen, slow-growing, very small acorns visible in autumn; its wood is used for martial-arts practice weapons (record says so). Leaflet numbers it 91, a single specimen on the map, east of the Jephson Memorial toward the Davis Clock Tower. No girth, height or planting date in any source seen; age left empty. Alive: council directory and 2024 leaflet list it as present, no dated photo of this tree found; flagged. Pin read off the numbered species map in the 2024 tree-walk leaflet (Royal Leamington Spa Town Council, Leamington in Bloom, Warwick District Council), calibrated against OSM/Commons positions of the Hitchman Fountain, Willes Obelisk, Jephson Memorial, Davis Clock Tower and Aviary (residual 3 to 8 m); expect 10 to 20 m error. Approximate, not a GPS fix. Recognition: stand at the foot of the steps and look up for a dark, glossy evergreen oak with narrow, toothed leaves (unlike the holm oaks nearby). Steps location is from the council text, not mapped by me.

name: The Caucasian Oak in Jephson Gardens

location.address: Jephson Gardens, Newbold Terrace / The Parade, Royal Leamington Spa

access: Free, public park (Green Flag, council-run), open daily; entrances on Newbold Terrace and The Parade. Opening hours not checked in this pass.
verify_notes: Council record: Quercus macranthera (Persian Oak), from the Caucasus; "a large, rare tree", notable for its height, with neighbouring trees still small though quite old; best seen from the path by the glasshouse. Leaflet number 93, one specimen on the map, about 25 m north of the Glasshouse (Commons/geograph place the Glasshouse at about 52.28788, -1.53200), consistent with the council wording. No girth, height or age in any source; age empty. Alive: listed in council directory and 2024 leaflet; no dated photo found; flagged. Approximate, not a GPS fix. Recognition: from the glasshouse path, the tall single-stemmed oak with large leaves standing above smaller trees.

location.address: Jephson Gardens, Newbold Terrace / The Parade, Royal Leamington Spa (path from the Aviary towards Willes Road)

access: Free, public park (Green Flag, council-run), open daily; entrances on Newbold Terrace and The Parade. Opening hours not checked in this pass.
verify_notes: Council record: several larger sweet gums in Jephson Gardens; the largest in Warwickshire is "along the path from the Aviary towards Willes Road" (superlative is the council's own, no measurement given; no Tree Register or champion listing found, TROBI not searched directly). Leaflet number 66 appears at several points; two marks about 7 m apart lie roughly 65 m east of the Aviary on that path (52.2888, -1.5293); I cannot tell from the map which is the largest, so the pin is the pair midpoint and the entry is one point. A third mark near 52.2893, -1.5288 is also on the east side. Leaflet says Sweet Gum and Sugar Maple give the deep reds of autumn colour in the gardens (best_time candidate: autumn colour, October to early November). No girth, height, age.
